guidelines: NICE Clinical Guidelines: Generalised Anxiety Disorder and Panic Disorder
assessment: Panic attacks involve acute sympathetic nervous system hyperarousal causing palpitations, hyperventilation, trembling, and a sense of impending doom.
immediateInterventions: 4-7-8 Rhythmic Breathing: Inhale through the nose for 4 seconds, hold for 7 seconds, exhale slowly through pursed lips for 8 seconds. Perform 4 cycles to stimulate parasympathetic vagal tone.
5-4-3-2-1 Sensory Grounding: Identify 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, and 1 you can taste to anchor nervous system awareness.
Somatic reassurance: Remind yourself that panic surges typically peak within 10 minutes and will pass.
redFlags: Chest pain radiating to arm/jaw, severe persistent shortness of breath, or thoughts of self-harm require immediate emergency assistance. National Mental Health Helpline (KIRAN India): 1800-599-0019 / Emergency: 112.

guidelines: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 757: Screening for Perinatal Depression / Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)
assessment: While 'baby blues' occur in up to 80% of mothers and resolve within 2 weeks, persistent sad mood, feelings of inadequacy, detachment from the infant, or debilitating insomnia beyond 2 weeks indicate Postpartum Depression.
supportActions: Screen using the EPDS self-assessment questionnaire.
Involve a trusted support person (partner, family member, doula) to take over night infant feedings for dedicated sleep blocks.
Consult an obstetrician or perinatal psychiatrist for evidence-based talk therapy (CBT, IPT) and medication options safe during lactation.
redFlags: Intrusive thoughts of harming oneself or the baby, hallucinations, or severe disorganization are psychiatric emergencies (Postpartum Psychosis). Call 112 immediately.
